clue.text: Italian barman hires drunk to catch sleazeball

indicators.note: to catch means one set of letters holds another inside it
drunk suggests the letters of hires are reeling into a new order

parts.note: a sleazeball is a pig, a disgusting person

explanation.surface: A bartender in Italy takes on a tipsy employee in order to trap a creep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges HIRES to RESHI, and 'to catch' puts PIG inside it. 'Barman' is no bartender: it is a composer, someone who writes bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottorino Respighi was an Italian composer, and a composer writes music in bars.

clue.text: Pervert names upmarket place of entertainment

indicators.note: to pervert is to twist or distort, so the letters of names upmarket are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A deviant gives his name to a posh venue for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pervert' looks like a noun for a person, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange NAMES UPMARKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair with rides and stalls is a site people visit for fun.

clue.text: Capital less quiet after translating a family of languages

indicators.note: translating means changing a text into another form, so these letters are turned into a new arrangement
less means a letter is subtracted from the word Capital

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A capital city grows quieter once its languages are translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes P from CAPITAL, leaving CAITAL, and 'after translating' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Altaic is a proposed grouping of Central Asian tongues including Turkic and Mongolic.

clue.text: Untouched instrument

definitions.meaning: pure, never handled or sexually experienced
a small box-shaped harpsichord of the 16th and 17th centuries

explanation.surface: An instrument nobody has ever played.
explanation.definitionFit: Untouched means chaste or pure, as a maiden is; a virginal is also a small early keyboard instrument like a harpsichord.

clue.text: Opposite boy, maiden

parts.note: Antony is a boy's name
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl sits facing a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A word meaning the reverse of another, such as hot and cold, is its opposite.

clue.text: Opening of chocolate bar, brilliant

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from chocolate

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: Unwrapping a chocolate bar is a brilliant moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant here means very smart or ingenious.

clue.text: See 1
See 24

parts.note: 20-down's answer can mean both a receptacle that holds things and a boat; this answer is two words, one for each of those senses

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue, with a query.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer joins a word for something that holds things and a word for a boat, the two senses of the answer at 20.
explanation.definitionFit: A freight ship carrying cargo boxes is a big seagoing craft, and both its parts name that other word's senses.

clue.text: Shapeless hot clothing pinkish at the edges

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so the word for hot goes outside the other letters

parts.note: hot can mean passionate, full of desire, i.e. amorous

indicators.note: the edges of pinkish are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A steamy outfit whose trim is a shade of pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' means lustful here, not warm: AMOROUS. 'clothing' wraps it round PH, the first and last letters of 'pinkish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no definite form or structure is formless.

clue.text: Good to poke eye, say, mostly, when back in trouble

indicators.note: to poke means pushing one letter into the middle of the others
back means the shortened word is read in reverse order
mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: an eye is an example of an organ of the body, as 'say' signals

explanation.surface: Someone talks of prodding an eye when things turn nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ORGAN to ORGA, 'when back' turns it to AGRO, and 'to poke' pushes G in.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive behaviour or hassle, which is bother.

clue.text: Drunkard taking stout regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of stout, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker who keeps ordering stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout is a dark beer, which suits the surface, but here it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual heavy drinker is a sot.

clue.text: Weapon's name recalled

indicators.note: recalled read as re-called: called back, so the word for name is read backwards

parts.note: a tag is a name or label, as in a name tag

explanation.surface: The name of a weapon is withdrawn from sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Weapon' is 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gat is slang for a handgun, a firearm.

clue.text: Accent put on resources keeping cutback at its limits

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the money word goes round the other letters

parts.note: money is financial resources

indicators.note: the limits of cutback are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone affects a voice to sound poorer while hoarding funds despite austerity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at its limits' gives CK, the first and last letters of 'cutback'. Mockney is a fake Cockney accent, Cockney being working-class London speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockney is a fake working-class London speech style adopted by middle-class people, so it is an affected way of talking.

clue.text: Bottom transformed is immaculate initially in Italian town

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream, Bottom the weaver is given a donkey's head, so he is turned into an ass

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of immaculate

explanation.surface: Someone's backside is changed and becomes spotless, in a town in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom transformed' looks like an anagram of BOTTOM, but it is Shakespeare's Bottom, turned into an ass.
explanation.definitionFit: Assisi is a hill town in Umbria, famous as the home of St Francis.

parts.note: 9-down's answer is two words, a holder and a boat; this word is also both a large drinking glass and a sailing boat

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue, with a query.
explanation.walkthrough: The query signals a pun: this word is both a large glass for sherry or beer (a container) and a sailing boat (a ship).
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is both a tall glass and a two-masted sailing craft, matching both halves of the other answer.

clue.text: Young and sexy in blue pants

indicators.note: pants as British slang for rubbish, poor, so the letters of in blue are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone looks youthful and alluring in blue underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear, but as slang for 'rubbish' it tells you to rearrange IN BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubile describes a young woman who is sexually attractive.

clue.text: Threat to children, poor golfer?

definitions.meaning: an imaginary monster used to scare youngsters into behaving
a bogey is a hole played one stroke over par, so someone who keeps scoring them is not much good

explanation.surface: A scary figure for kids turns out to be a hopeless golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogeyman is a monster used to frighten kids; a bogey is one over par in golf, so a 'bogey man' scores badly.

clue.text: Inspiring love, witch mounted soldier

indicators.note: inspiring read literally as breathing in, so the witch word takes a letter inside it

parts.note: a dragon is a fierce, unpleasant woman, as a witch is
love is zero in tennis, giving the letter O

explanation.surface: A soldier on horseback, moved by love for a witch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' means breathing in here: DRAGON takes in O.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a cavalryman, originally one carrying a short musket.

clue.text: Boat nonetheless eventually capsizing, though not entirely

indicators.note: capsizing says the hidden letters are read backwards
though not entirely says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boat finally turns over, but only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizing' suits a boat, but it is the signal to read LESSEV, from 'nonetheless eventually', backwards; it sits in a down clue, where reading upward is natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any ship or boat.

clue.text: Find another place to stir round what?

indicators.note: round means the stir word is placed around the other letters

parts.note: to rouse is to stir someone up
eh? is a way of saying what? when you have not heard

explanation.surface: Someone asks why they should stir round, and to what end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts ROUSE around EH, the 'what?' you say when you mishear.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehouse people is to give them a new home elsewhere.

clue.text: Throw Austen out of joint

indicators.note: out of joint means dislocated, so the letters of Austen are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone flings a novel by Jane Austen across the room in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' is the definition, in the sense of a horse throwing its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a rider is to unseat them, knocking them off a horse.

clue.text: Architect drops in to see dog

indicators.note: drops means letting go of part of the word, so a run of letters is removed

parts.note: Augustus Pugin was the Victorian Gothic Revival architect who designed much of the Houses of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: An architect pops in to visit a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops in' looks like a visit, but 'drops' removes IN from PUGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pug is a small flat-faced breed of hound.

clue.text: Fixture around the neck?

definitions.meaning: a scheduled sporting match, as in a cup draw
something worn at the collar, a necktie

explanation.surface: Something fixed round someone's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a sports fixture, especially a cup match; a tie is also a necktie, worn round the collar.

clue.text: Tom captivated by tongue on feline that's very much appreciated

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive inside another word, so Tom's surname sits within the language

parts.note: a tongue is a language; Tamil is spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka
Tom Hanks is the Hollywood actor, so Tom gives his surname
a lion is a big cat, a feline

explanation.surface: A cat captures a tom by the tongue, much to its owner's appreciation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a male cat to go with 'feline', but it is the actor Tom Hanks. 'captivated by' puts HANKS inside TAMIL, and 'on' joins LION after it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an emphatic expression of gratitude, said when someone has been extremely helpful.

clue.text: Vulgar square?

definitions.meaning: twelve dozen, 144, the square of twelve

explanation.surface: Is a coarse person also a fuddy-duddy?
explanation.definitionFit: Gross means crude or coarse; a gross is 144, the number twelve squared.

clue.text: Those pressurised to ask for help during hospital investigations

indicators.note: during means going on within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: scans are medical imaging investigations in a hospital
to pray is to ask a higher power for help

explanation.surface: Patients under stress pray for help while undergoing hospital tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those pressurised' sounds like stressed people, but means aerosol cans under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerosols for paint or graffiti hold their contents under pressure.

clue.text: Notedly dramatic explosion in apricot pie, not good

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters are blown into a new order
not means the word for good is taken away from apricot pie

parts.note: pi is short for pious, i.e. good

explanation.surface: An apricot pie blows up in the oven, which is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' removes PI (pious) from APRICOT PIE, leaving ARCOTPIE, which 'explosion' rearranges. 'Notedly' means in musical notes: dramatic in the way of opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic means over-the-top and theatrical, as in opera, a drama sung in musical notes.

clue.text: Lift innards of calf as wild animal

parts.note: a jack is a device for lifting a car

indicators.note: the innards of calf are its middle letters, dropping the first and last

explanation.surface: Someone hoists the guts of a calf as a wild beast would.
explanation.walkthrough: A jackal is a scavenger, so innards of a calf fit the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackal is a wild dog of Africa and Asia.
